name: PinguinoLink
desc: Secure device link: Tailscale status, remote OBS macros, device pairing, file send/receive (Windows + macOS)

help.title: OBS WebSocket password
help.summary: The password Link uses to talk to OBS on this PC. It is stored in the key vault, never in a file or log.
steps: In OBS open Tools > WebSocket Server Settings.
Tick Enable WebSocket server and keep the port at 4455.
Tick Enable Authentication. Click Show Connect Info to see or change the Server Password.
Copy that password and paste it into the box next to this key (Set / Rotate).
If you rotate it in OBS later, set it here again.
help.example: A random string of letters and digits (format only)

_module.title: PinguinoLink
_module.summary: Links your devices: shows Tailscale status, runs OBS macros (scene, start/stop stream, mute), pairs other PCs so they share the master role, and sends files.
steps: Install Tailscale on every device and sign in with the same account. Link only talks over Tailscale.
Streaming PC: start OBS with the WebSocket server enabled (Tools > WebSocket Server Settings), then put its password in the key vault as OBS_WS_PASSWORD.
Open the Link page. In Devices, click Show a pairing code on one device. On the other, type the first device's Tailscale name and the code, press Pair, then click Allow on the first.
Macros (BRB, live, start, stop, mute) run in OBS. Their scene and input names must match your OBS names exactly; edit them in the Link config file.
To redo setup: unpair a device in the Devices card, or restart Link from Modules.

obs.title: OBS WebSocket
obs.summary: Link must reach OBS on this PC (127.0.0.1:4455) to run macros and to check that your scenes exist.
steps: Make sure OBS is running.
In OBS open Tools > WebSocket Server Settings and tick Enable WebSocket server (port 4455).
If Authentication is on, store its password in the key vault as OBS_WS_PASSWORD (Set / Rotate).

The check says exactly one thing: OBS is not running / OBS asks for a password but none is stored / OBS rejected the stored password / OK. Press Test next to the key in Integrations > Key vault to re-run just this check.
Do not forward port 4455 on your router; OBS is only reachable from this PC.

macros.title: OBS macro targets
macros.summary: Each macro names a scene or audio input. This check confirms those names exist in OBS right now.
steps: The default macros use scene 'BRB', scene 'Main' and input 'Mic/Aux'. They are guesses until you match them to your OBS.
Compare the names listed in this check with OBS (Scenes box and Audio Mixer). Names are case-sensitive.
Either rename the scene/input in OBS, or edit the macro in the Link config file (macros section) to use your name.
Restart Link after editing the config. This check turns green when every name matches.

tailscale.title: Tailscale
tailscale.summary: Link talks to your other devices only through Tailscale. Without it this PC works alone: local OBS macros still run, remote control and pairing do not.
steps: Install Tailscale from the link below if it is missing.
Open the Tailscale app and sign in with the same account on every device.
Status Stopped means the Tailscale app is closed or turned off: click its tray icon and turn it on.
Green means Tailscale is running and shows how many devices are online.

hub.title: Hub device
hub.summary: On a client PC, OBS macros are forwarded to the hub (the streaming PC). The hub must be online on your tailnet.
steps: Check the streaming PC is on, has Tailscale running and Link started.
The hub name in the Link config (hub) must equal its Tailscale device name.
A relayed path works but adds delay; direct is best (same network or good NAT).

role.title: Role: hub or client
role.summary: The hub is the PC that runs OBS and executes macros itself. A client forwards macros to the hub.
steps: On the streaming PC the role should be hub; on every other PC it should be client.
Changing the role is done in the Link config file (role) and takes effect after a Link restart. Change it only on purpose.
A warning here on a client is normal: it just tells you macros will go to the hub.

mesh.title: Device mesh
mesh.summary: Shows paired devices. With none paired, this PC runs alone and is its own master.
steps: Open the Link page > Devices.
On one PC click Show a pairing code. On the other PC enter the first PC's Tailscale name and the code, then press Pair.
Click Allow on the first PC when asked. The code works once and expires after 5 minutes.
